findings: src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp TryDenseFilterSelection: the conditions are general. It covers numeric physical types, flat vectors, and AND/OR trees of =, <>, <, >, <=, >= and BETWEEN between column ref #0 and non-NULL constants of exactly the column's LogicalType (so DECIMAL width and scale must match too). Nothing in it names tables, columns, literals or data sizes. Any single-column disjunctive range or equality filter qualifies.
NULL handling is correct. The tree has no NOT, so a NULL row can never pass, and validity is applied at the end with the original row index.

scan_count > STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE is handled safely. The dense path only requires approved_tuple_count <= 2048. Row indices beyond 2048 are gathered from the full-size vector and validity, which is valid memory. The bitmap OR fallback checks that every index is < STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE and otherwise uses the old loop.

Float and double semantics match the executor because the code uses the same Equals/LessThan/... operator templates, including NaN ordering. The constant's type is checked against the column type before GetValueUnsafe<T>. The ConstantFilter children inside conjunctions make the same type assumption as the existing TemplatedFilterSelection path.
In the bitmap union, later children are evaluated only on rows not yet matched. For an OR this gives the same set as before, the output stays in input order, and there are no duplicates.
Stack buffers are bounded: at most a few 2KB masks per recursion level, plus one gather buffer of 2048*sizeof(T), which is 32KB for hugeint. That is acceptable.
